scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
This freight brokerage's technology cost structure has become a liability sitting directly under your DOT compliance deadline. Your $1,850,000 annual spend is anchored to 28 SQL Server instances and 620 Hyper-V virtual machines that require constant licensing renewals, hardware refresh cycles, and dedicated administration — costs that recur whether or not the systems are audit-ready. With your compliance audit opening in six months, this is the moment to convert that fixed overhead into a controlled, trackable programme investment rather than absorbing another year of the same spend while hoping the current environment holds up under scrutiny. Migrating load-matching and carrier-settlement systems to Google Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL directly addresses both of your performance measures: it replaces capital-intensive, self-managed infrastructure with consumption-based compute and a managed database layer that carries built-in automated backups, point-in-time recovery, and audit logging — capabilities that materially strengthen your compliance posture ahead of the audit rather than working against its timeline.

Over the 2-year, $4,200,000 programme, you should expect a phased migration that keeps carrier settlement and load-matching operational throughout, with early phases prioritizing the data layer and compliance-relevant audit trails so DOT readiness improves well before the six-month window closes, not after. Financially, plan for near-term costs to run alongside your existing on-premises spend during transition, with the annual run-rate reduction — driven by eliminated Hyper-V licensing, reduced administrative headcount needs, and right-sized compute — materializing predominantly in year two as legacy infrastructure is decommissioned. I recommend you request a phase-gated cost and compliance milestone review at the 90-day mark, giving you an early, evidence-based checkpoint on both the audit-readiness trajectory and the trajectory toward reducing your $1,850,000 baseline, well before either commitment is fully at stake.
